stem: According to the passage, why does a young tree provide little shade?
options: It is usually planted in streets with limited sunlight.
Its roots have not yet reached water deep in the soil.
It has not yet grown enough to develop a broad crown.
Its leaves release too much water vapour into the air.

verdicts.working: The passage says a young tree provides little shade before trees mature; the best explanation is that it has not developed a broad crown.

working: The passage states that a young tree provides little shade and that trees need years to mature; its crown has not yet grown large.
solution: A young tree provides little shade because it has not yet matured enough to develop a broad crown.
